subject: Linguistics
title: Speech Planning
description: A fast breakdown of Speech Planning for builders.

hook.text: Before you say a word, your brain selects a concept, picks a word, and plans every muscle movement.

buildup.text: Speech production involves four stages: message, words, sounds, then articulation.

discovery.text: Levelt's model shows these stages run in a cascade—you're planning the next word while saying this one.

twist.text: The whole process takes about 600 milliseconds from thought to spoken word.

climax.text: Speakers coordinate over 100 muscles in the mouth, throat, and lungs for each syllable.

punchline.text: Speaking is the most complex motor task humans perform—effortlessly.

quiz.question: How long does speech planning take from thought to word?
